title: Set the screen brightness to the maximum

source.changes: Instruction is the source's goal, word for word. The source set nothing up, so a phone already at full brightness passed with no action; here setup keeps the phone's own brightness and auto-brightness, turns auto-brightness off and starts at 128, and teardown puts both back. The check is the source's (screen_brightness at least 255), read with `settings get` instead of the source's helper.

setup.why: Keep the phone's own auto-brightness mode and brightness once (a retried setup keeps the first copy), so teardown puts them back.

argv: f=/data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.orig; [ -e $f ] || { settings get system screen_brightness_mode; settings get system screen_brightness; } > $f

setup.why: Start with auto-brightness off and the brightness in the middle (128 of 255), so the agent has to raise it.

argv: settings put system screen_brightness_mode 0 && settings put system screen_brightness 128

setup.why: Open Settings at its home page, whatever screen an earlier run left it on.

instruction: Set the brightness to the maximum level.

checks.why: The system brightness setting is at least 255, the source's maximum (phones whose scale goes higher pass too). Setup left 128, so an agent that does nothing fails.

teardown.why: Put the phone's own brightness and auto-brightness mode back, and drop the saved copy.

argv: f=/data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.orig; m=$(sed -n 1p $f 2>/dev/null); b=$(sed -n 2p $f 2>/dev/null); case "$b" in ''|*[!0-9]*) ;; *) settings put system screen_brightness $b ;; esac; case "$m" in 0|1) settings put system screen_brightness_mode $m ;; esac; rm -f $f

oracle.why: Write the maximum, as dragging the slider to the end does.
